sentences.t: Gwyr Gwyned a ymchweles dracheuyn yn llawen orawenus.
sentences.l: The men of-Gwynedd it-was-that returned back joyful exultant.
sentences.i: The men of Gwynedd went home again, glad and exultant.
sentences.n: The abnormal sentence again: the subject first (Gwyr Gwyned 'the men of Gwynedd'), then the particle a, then the verb. ymchweles 'returned', 3 sg. preterite (-es) of ymchwelut: after a fronted noun subject the verb stays singular even when the noun is plural. dracheuyn ← tracheuyn 'back again', softened as an adverb. yn llawen orawenus 'glad, exultant': adverbial yn; orawenus ← gorawenus 'elated, jubilant', softened as the second adjective of the pair.

sentences.t: “Arglwyd,” heb y Guydyon wrth Uath, “ponyt oed iawn ynni ollwng eu dylyedauc y wyr y Deheu, a wystlyssant in ar tangneued? Ac ny dylywn y garcharu.”
sentences.l: “Lord,” said Gwydion to Math, “would-it-not-be right for-us to-release their nobleman to the men of the South, whom they-pledged to-us on peace? And we-ought-not his imprisoning.”
sentences.i: “Lord,” said Gwydion to Math, “would it not be right for us to release their nobleman to the men of the South, whom they gave us as a pledge for the peace? We ought not to keep him in prison.”
sentences.n: heb y Guydyon 'said Gwydion' (heb y before a name); Guydyon is Gwydion, spelled with gu here and Gwydyon in Goewin's speech below, both kept as Evans prints them. wrth Uath ← Math, softened after wrth 'to'. ponyt 'is it not', the negative question; oed here is 'would be'. iawn 'right' (as an adjective; as a noun below, 'amends, redress'). ynni 'for us', y 'to' conjugated (1 pl.). ollwng ← gollwng 'release', softened because words stand between iawn and it. dylyedauc 'nobleman, man of birth' (from dylyet 'right, entitlement'): the hostage Gwrgi Gwastra of the last part. y wyr ← gwyr 'men', softened after y 'to'. a wystlyssant 'whom they pledged': wystlyssant ← gwystlyssant, 3 pl. preterite of gwystlaw, softened after a. in 'to us', a short form of ynni. ar tangneued 'on peace', as surety for it. ny dylywn 'we ought not', 1 pl. present of dylyu. y garcharu 'his imprisoning', to imprison him: karcharu softened after y 'his', the object before the verbal noun.

sentences.t: “Rydhaer ynteu,” heb y Math.
sentences.l: “Let-him-be-freed then,” said Math.
sentences.i: “Then let him be freed,” said Math.
sentences.n: Rydhaer 'let (him) be freed': the impersonal present subjunctive (-er) of rydhau 'set free' (modern rhyddhau; r is written for rh), used as a command with no person named. ynteu here is the adverb 'then, in that case', the same word as the pronoun ynteu 'he for his part'.

sentences.t: A'r guas hwnnw, a'r gwystlon oed gyt ac ef, a ellyngwyt yn ol guyr y Deheu.
sentences.l: And that young-man, and the hostages that-were with him, it-was-that were-released after the men of the South.
sentences.i: So that young man, and the hostages who were with him, were let go after the men of the South.
sentences.n: A'r: a 'and' + yr 'the'. guas 'young man, youth' (later 'servant'). oed gyt ac ef 'who were with him': a relative clause with the particle unwritten. a ellyngwyt 'were released': ellyngwyt ← gellyngwyt, the impersonal preterite (-wyt) of gellwng/gollwng, softened after a. The impersonal names no doer, 'one released'. yn ol 'after'. guyr is gwyr 'men'.

sentences.t: Enteu Math a gyrchwys Caer Tathyl.
sentences.l: He-for-his-part Math it-was-that made-for Caer Dathyl.
sentences.i: Math, for his part, made for Caer Dathyl.
sentences.n: Enteu is ynteu 'he for his part', so spelled here and in the next sentence but one, with e for y as in e ystauell, e hutlath. a gyrchwys 'made for': gyrchwys ← kyrchwys, 3 sg. preterite (-wys) of kyrchu 'make for, go to', softened after a. Caer Tathyl: Evans prints T, as in col. 86; Caer Dathyl elsewhere. The place is the same.

sentences.t: Giluaethwy uab Don a'r teulu a uuassynt gyt ac ef a gyrchyssant y gylchaw Gwyned mal y gnotayssynt, a heb gyrchu y llys.
sentences.l: Gilfaethwy son of-Dôn and the household-troop that had-been with him it-was-that made-for round-about Gwynedd as they-had-been-wont, and without making-for the court.
sentences.i: Gilfaethwy son of Dôn and the warband who had been with him went off on the circuit of Gwynedd, as they had been used to do, without going to the court.
sentences.n: uab ← mab 'son', softened after a name. a uuassynt 'that had been': uuassynt ← buassynt, the pluperfect (-assynt) of bot, softened after a. a gyrchyssant 'made for', 3 pl. preterite of kyrchu, softened. y gylchaw 'round about' (y + kylch 'circle'), the circuit Gilfaethwy made for Math in part 011. mal y gnotayssynt 'as they had been wont': gnotayssynt, the pluperfect (-ayssynt) of gnotau 'be accustomed'; y is the verbal particle. heb gyrchu 'without making for': kyrchu softened after heb.

sentences.t: Enteu Uath a gyrchwys e ystauell, ac a beris kyweiraw lle idaw y benelinyaw, ual y caei dodi y draet ym plyc croth y uorwyn.
sentences.l: He-for-his-part Math it-was-that made-for his chamber, and that caused preparing a-place for-him to recline, so-that he-might-get to-put his feet in-the-fold of-the-lap of-the maiden.
sentences.i: Math went to his chamber and had a couch made ready for him to recline on, so that he could set his feet in the fold of the maiden's lap.
sentences.n: Here are four of the five jobs of y in one sentence: y benelinyaw 'to recline', y 'to' (softening penelinyaw, from penelin 'elbow'); ual y caei, the verbal particle; y draet 'his feet', y 'his' (softening traet); y uorwyn 'the maiden', the article (softening morwyn, feminine). The fifth, y 'in', is in i'th below. Enteu Uath: Math softened after Enteu, though two sentences back Enteu Math is unsoftened; the scribe is not consistent. e ystauell 'his chamber': e for y. a beris ← peris, preterite of peri 'cause', softened after a. kyweiraw 'prepare'. caei: Evans prints caṛei with the r dotted beneath, the scribe's cancellation, so the r is left out; caei is the imperfect subjunctive of cael 'get, be able' (Red Book kaffei). ym plyc croth 'in the fold of the lap', as in part 011.

sentences.t: “Arglwyd,” heb y Goewyn, “keis uorwyn a uo is dy draet weithon. Gwreic wyf i.”
sentences.l: “Lord,” said Goewin, “seek a-maiden who may-be beneath your feet now. A-woman am I.”
sentences.i: “Lord,” said Goewin, “seek a maiden to be beneath your feet from now on. I am a woman.”
sentences.n: Goewyn is so spelled here, as in col. 87; Goewin in col. 82. keis 'seek', 2 sg. imperative of keissaw. uorwyn ← morwyn, softened as the object. a uo 'who may be': uo ← bo, present subjunctive of bot, softened after a. is 'below'. dy draet ← traet after dy 'your'. weithon 'now, henceforth' (gweith 'time' + hon 'this'), always written in this softened form. Gwreic wyf i 'a woman am I': the predicate first. gwreic is both 'woman' and 'wife'; she means she is no longer a virgin, the condition of her office.

sentences.t: “Pa ystyr yw hynny?”
sentences.l: “What meaning is that?”
sentences.i: “What does that mean?”
sentences.n: Math's question, without a tag. Pa ystyr 'what meaning': ystyr 'sense, meaning'. yw 'is'.

sentences.t: “Kyrch, Arglwyd, a doeth am uym penn, a hynny yn diargel, ac ny buum distaw inheu. Ny bu yn y llys nys guypei. Sef a doeth, dy nyeint ueibon dy chwaer, Arglwyd, Gwydyon uab Don a Giluaethwy uab Don.
sentences.l: “An-onset, Lord, it-was-that came upon my head, and that secretly, and I-was-not silent I-for-my-part. There-was-not in the court who-did-not-know-it. That-is who came: your nephews, sons of your sister, Lord, Gwydion son of Dôn and Gilfaethwy son of Dôn.
sentences.i: “An assault, Lord, came upon me, and that in secret; but I did not keep silent. There was no one in the court who did not know of it. Those who came were your nephews, your sister's sons, Lord: Gwydion son of Dôn and Gilfaethwy son of Dôn.
sentences.n: Kyrch 'an onset, an attack', the noun from kyrchu. am uym penn 'about my head', upon me: uym is uy 'my' with the nasal mutation written on it; penn keeps its p in the spelling. yn diargel 'secretly': diargel 'hidden, secret', from argel 'concealment' with di- strengthening it, not negating it (the Red Book has yn dirgel, the same sense); the deed was done in secret, but she made it known. ny buum 'I was not', 1 sg. preterite of bot. inheu 'I for my part'. Ny bu … nys guypei 'there was not (one) … who did not know it': nys is ny + the infixed 's 'it'; guypei is the imperfect subjunctive of gwybot. Sef a doeth 'that is who came'. nyeint 'nephews', plural of nei; ueibon ← meibon 'sons', softened in apposition.

sentences.t: A threis arnaf a orugant, a chywilyd y titheu, a chyscu a wnaethpwyt genhyf, a hynny i'th ystauell ac i'th wely.”
sentences.l: And violence upon-me they-did, and shame to you-for-your-part, and sleeping was-done with-me, and that in your chamber and in your bed.”
sentences.i: They did me violence, and you shame, and I was lain with, and that in your chamber and in your bed.”
sentences.n: A threis ← treis 'force, violence, rape', spirant mutation after a 'and'; it stands first and a orugant 'they did' (3 pl. preterite of gwneuthur) closes the clause. a chywilyd ← kywilyd 'shame', spirant after a; y titheu 'to you for your part'. chyscu ← kyscu 'sleep', spirant after a; a wnaethpwyt 'was done', the impersonal preterite of gwneuthur. genhyf 'with me', gan conjugated (1 sg.). i'th is y 'in' + 'th 'your', the fifth job of y; wely ← gwely 'bed', softened after 'th.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb ynteu, “yr hynn a allaf i, mi a baraf iawn y ti yn gyntaf, ac yn ol uy iawn y bydaf inheu.
sentences.l: “Yes,” said he-for-his-part, “what I-can I, I it-is-that will-cause amends to you first, and after my redress I-will-be I-for-my-part.
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said, “as far as I can, I will have amends made to you first, and afterwards I will go after my own.
sentences.n: yr hynn a allaf i 'what I can': in the White Book this clause has no verb of its own. The Red Book reads yr hynn a allaf mi ae gwnaf, mi a baraf itt gael iawn 'what I can, I will do it; I will make you get redress'; the scribe probably skipped from one mi a … to the next. The missing words are not supplied, and the clause reads as 'as far as I can'. a baraf ← paraf, 1 sg. present-future of peri 'cause', softened after a. iawn here is the noun 'amends, redress' (part 011: uy iawn 'my redress'). yn ol uy iawn y bydaf inheu 'after my amends I will be': yn ol is both 'after' and 'in pursuit of', so 'I will be after my own redress'. bydaf, 1 sg. present-future of bot.

sentences.t: A thitheu,” heb ef, “mi a'th gymeraf yn wreic im, ac a rodaf uedyant uyg kyuoeth i'th law ditheu.”
sentences.l: And you-for-your-part,” said he, “I it-is-that will-take-you as wife to-me, and that will-give the-power of-my realm into your hand you-for-your-part.”
sentences.i: And you,” he said, “I will take as my wife, and I will put the rule of my realm into your hand.”
sentences.n: A thitheu ← titheu 'you for your part', spirant after a. a'th gymeraf 'I will take you': 'th, the infixed object 'you', softens kymeraf. yn wreic ← gwreic, after the predicative yn. im 'to me'. a rodaf 'I will give' (rodi). uedyant ← medyant 'power, rule', softened as the object. uyg kyuoeth 'my realm': the nasal mutation of uy written as g, the k left plain. i'th law ← llaw, softened after 'th; ditheu ← titheu, softened after the possessive.

sentences.t: Ac yn hynny ny doethant wy yng kyuyl y llys, namyn trigyaw y gylchaw y wlat a wnaethant, yny aeth guahard udunt ar y bwyt a'y llynn.
sentences.l: And in that they-came-not they into-the-neighbourhood of the court, but staying round-about the land they-did, until went a-ban to-them on his food and his drink.
sentences.i: Meanwhile they did not come near the court, but stayed going round the country, until a ban went out against them on his food and drink.
sentences.n: yn hynny 'in that (time)', meanwhile. ny doethant wy 'they did not come'. yng kyuyl 'into the neighbourhood of': yn + kyuyl, the nasal written ng, the k left plain. trigyaw y gylchaw y wlat a wnaethant 'staying round about the land they did': verbal noun, then a wnaethant (3 pl. of gwneuthur). y wlat ← gwlat, softened after the feminine article. yny 'until'. guahard 'prohibition, ban'. udunt 'to them', y conjugated (3 pl.). ar y bwyt a'y llynn 'on his food and his drink': a'y is a 'and' + 'y 'his' (the Red Book writes a'e, which can only be the possessive), so both y's are 'his': they are barred from Math's food and drink, the provision they lived on while making his circuit.

sentences.t: Yn gyntaf ny doethant wy yn y gyuyl ef.
sentences.l: At-first they-came-not they into his neighbourhood he.
sentences.i: At first they did not come near him.
sentences.n: yn y gyuyl ef 'into his neighbourhood': kyuyl softened after y 'his', and ef after the noun repeats 'his'. The sentence goes back over the time before they came.

sentences.t: Yna y doethant wynteu attaw ef.
sentences.l: Then it-was they-came they-for-their-part to-him he.
sentences.i: Then they came to him.
sentences.n: Yna y doethant: the adverb first, then the particle y and the verb. wynteu 'they for their part'. attaw 'to him', at conjugated (3 sg. masc.).

sentences.t: “Arglwyd,” heb wynt, “dyd da it.”
sentences.l: “Lord,” said they, “day good to-you.”
sentences.i: “Lord,” they said, “good day to you.”
sentences.n: heb wynt 'said they': Evans prints wyn with a raised t, brought into the line here. dyd da it 'good day to you': it 'to you', y 'to' conjugated (2 sg.).

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb ynteu, “ay y wneuthur iawn ymi y doethauch chwi?”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said he-for-his-part, “is-it to make amends to-me that you-came you?”
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said, “is it to make me amends that you have come?”
sentences.n: ay asks a question about the phrase it puts first: 'is it to …?'. y wneuthur 'to make': gwneuthur softened after y 'to'. iawn 'amends'. ymi 'to me', y conjugated (1 sg.). y doethauch 'you came', 2 pl. preterite of dyuot, after the particle y.

sentences.t: “Arglwyd, i'th ewyllus yd ydym.”
sentences.l: “Lord, in your will it-is we-are.”
sentences.i: “Lord, we are at your will.”
sentences.n: i'th 'in your' (y 'in' + 'th). ewyllus 'will'. yd ydym 'we are': yd is the particle before a vowel after a fronted phrase; ydym, 1 pl. present of bot.

sentences.t: “Bei uy ewyllwys, ny chollwn o wyr ac arueu a golleis. Vyg kywilyd ny ellwch chwi y dalu y mi, heb angheu Pryderi. A chan doethauch chwitheu y'm ewyllus inheu, mi a dechreuaf boen arnawch.”
sentences.l: “Were-it my will, I-would-not-have-lost of men and arms what I-lost. My shame you-cannot you its paying to me, besides the-death of-Pryderi. And since you-came you-for-your-part to my will I-for-my-part, I it-is-that will-begin punishment on-you.”
sentences.i: “If it were my will, I would not have lost the men and arms I lost. My shame you cannot repay me, to say nothing of Pryderi's death. And since you have come to my will, I shall begin your punishment.”
sentences.n: Bei 'were it', the imperfect subjunctive of bot, used for 'if'. ewyllwys: so spelled here, ewyllus just before and after. ny chollwn 'I would not have lost': collwn, imperfect (subjunctive) 1 sg. of colli, with spirant after ny. o wyr ac arueu 'of men and arms': gwyr softened after o; arueu as Evans prints it (Red Book arueu; the second witness's araeu is its own typo). a golleis 'that I lost', colleis (1 sg. preterite) softened after a. Vyg kywilyd 'my shame', the object put first; Vyg is uyg 'my'. ny ellwch ← gellwch, 2 pl. present of gallu, softened after ny. y dalu 'its paying': talu softened after y 'its'. heb 'without, apart from', here 'not counting'. chan ← can 'since', spirant after a. y'm 'to my'. boen ← poen 'pain, punishment', softened as the object. arnawch 'on you', ar conjugated (2 pl.).

sentences.t: Ac yna y kymerth e hutlath, ac y trewis Giluathwy yny uyd daran ewic; ac achub y llall a wnaeth yn gyflym, kyt mynhei dianc nys gallei, a'y taraw a'r un hutlath yny uyd yn garw.
sentences.l: And then he-took his magic-rod, and he-struck Gilfaethwy until he-is daran(?) a-hind; and seizing the other he-did quickly, though he-would-wish to-escape he-could-not-it, and his striking with the same magic-rod until he-is a stag.
sentences.i: And then he took his magic rod and struck Gilfaethwy, so that he became a hind; and he seized the other quickly (though he wanted to escape, he could not), and struck him with the same rod, so that he became a stag.
sentences.n: y kymerth 'he took', preterite of kymryt. e hutlath 'his magic rod': e for y 'his'; hutlath is hut 'magic' + llath 'rod, staff, yard'. It is usually taken as a wand; what kind of rod is meant is not certain. Giluathwy: so spelled here (col. 90); Giluaethwy elsewhere. y trewis 'he struck', 3 sg. preterite of taraw. yny uyd 'until he is': uyd ← byd, the present-future of bot, softened after yny, used in narrative for 'until he became'. daran: so Evans, plainly (col. 90 l. 29); the Red Book has yny uyd yn daran ewic, so daran is a word of its own standing before ewic, not a slip for yn, and it is the White Book that lacks yn (compare yny uyd yn garw below). What daran means here is unknown; the translation leaves it out. achub 'seize'. kyt mynhei 'though he would wish': mynhei, imperfect subjunctive of mynnu, after kyt 'though'. nys gallei 'he could not (do) it': nys = ny + 's 'it'. a'y taraw 'and his striking', struck him: after 'y 'his' one expects daraw (as in A'y daraw in col. 92), but the t is written unsoftened (the Red Book has ae daraw here). yn garw ← carw, softened after yn.

sentences.t: “Canys ywch yn rwymedigaeth, mi a wnaf ywch gerdet y gyt, a'ch bot yn gymaredic, ac yn un anyan a'r gwyduilot yd ywch yn eu rith; ac yn yr amser y bo etiued udunt wy, y uot ywchwitheu.
sentences.l: “Since you-are in bond, I it-is-that will-make to-you walk together, and your being mated, and of one nature with the wild-beasts that you-are in their form; and in the time that there-may-be offspring to-them they, its being to-you-for-your-part.
sentences.i: “Since you are under bond, I will make you go together and be mated, and be of one nature with the wild beasts whose shape you wear; and at the season when they have young, so shall you.
sentences.n: Canys 'since'. ywch 'you are' (2 pl. of bot, as in yd ywch below); rwymedigaeth 'bond, obligation' (rhwymedigaeth, r for rh): they are bound, having come to his will. mi a wnaf ywch gerdet 'I will make you walk': gwneuthur y + person + verbal noun is 'make (someone) do'; ywch here is 'to you', y conjugated (2 pl.); gerdet ← kerdet, softened. y gyt 'together'. a'ch bot 'and your being'. yn gymaredic ← kymaredic 'mated, paired' (kymar 'mate'), softened after yn. un anyan 'one nature'. gwyduilot 'wild beasts': gwyd 'wild' + mil 'animal' (softened to uil in the compound), with the plural ending -ot; whether it means deer in particular or any wild animal is disputed. yn eu rith 'in their shape'. etiued 'offspring'. y bo 'there may be', present subjunctive. y uot ← bot, softened after y 'its'. ywchwitheu is ywch 'to you' + chwitheu 'you for your part', written as one word.

sentences.t: A blwydyn y hediw dowch yma atafi.”
sentences.l: And a-year from today come here to-me.”
sentences.i: And a year from today, come here to me.”
sentences.n: blwydyn y hediw 'a year from today': hediw 'today'. dowch 'come', 2 pl. imperative of dyuot. atafi is ataf i 'to me', at conjugated (1 sg.) with the pronoun joined on.

sentences.t: Ym penn y ulwydyn o'r un dyd, llyma y clywei odorun adan paret yr ystauell, a chyuarthua cwn y llys am penn y godorun.
sentences.l: At the end of the year of the same day, behold he-heard an-uproar under the wall of the chamber, and the baying of the dogs of the court about the head of the uproar.
sentences.i: At the end of the year, to the day, he heard an uproar beneath the chamber wall, and the court's dogs baying over the uproar.
sentences.n: Ym penn 'at the head, at the end of'. y ulwydyn ← blwydyn, softened after the feminine article. o'r un dyd 'of the same day', to the day. llyma 'behold'. y clywei 'he heard', imperfect of clywet. odorun ← godorun 'din, uproar', softened as the object; y godorun at the end keeps the g (the noun is masculine). adan 'under'. paret 'wall' (modern pared). a chyuarthua ← kyuarthua 'barking, baying', spirant after a. am penn 'about the head of', over and around.

sentences.t: “Edrych,” heb ynteu, “beth yssyd allan.”
sentences.l: “Look,” said he-for-his-part, “what there-is outside.”
sentences.i: “Look,” he said, “and see what is outside.”
sentences.n: Edrych 'look', 2 sg. imperative. beth 'what' (← peth 'thing'). yssyd 'that is', the relative form of bot.

sentences.t: “Arglwyd,” heb un, “mi a edrycheis. Mae yna carw, ac ewic, ac elein gyt ac wynt.”
sentences.l: “Lord,” said one, “I it-is-that looked. There-is there a-stag, and a-hind, and a-fawn with them.”
sentences.i: “Lord,” said one, “I have looked. There is a stag out there, and a hind, and a fawn with them.”
sentences.n: heb un 'said one (of them)'. mi a edrycheis 'I looked', 1 sg. preterite (-eis). Mae yna 'there is there'. elein 'fawn, young deer'. gyt ac wynt 'with them'.

sentences.t: Ac ar hynny kyuodi a oruc ynteu a dyuot allan.
sentences.l: And on that rising he-did he-for-his-part and coming out.
sentences.i: At that he rose and came out.
sentences.n: kyuodi a oruc ynteu 'rising he did': the verbal noun closed by a oruc, then a dyuot 'and coming' carries on. ar hynny 'on that, thereupon'.

sentences.t: A phan doeth, sef y guelei y trillydyn; sef trillydyn eodynt, carw, ac ewic, ac elein cryf.
sentences.l: And when he-came, that-is he-saw the three-beasts; that-is the-three-beasts they-were: a-stag, and a-hind, and a-strong fawn.
sentences.i: And when he came, what he saw was the three beasts; and the three beasts were these: a stag, a hind, and a sturdy fawn.
sentences.n: A phan ← pan 'when', spirant after a. sef y guelei 'that is, he saw'. trillydyn 'three beasts': tri + llydyn 'beast', the numeral taking a singular noun. eodynt: a scribal slip for oedynt 'they were', the letters transposed (Red Book oedynt); certain on the image, kept as written. cryf 'strong'.

sentences.t: Sef a wnaeth, dyrchauael e hutlath.
sentences.l: That-is what he-did: raising his magic-rod.
sentences.i: What he did was raise his magic rod.
sentences.n: Sef a wnaeth 'what he did', answered by the verbal noun dyrchauael 'raising'. e hutlath: e for y 'his', as before.

sentences.t: “Yr hwnn a uu ohonawch yn ewic yrllyned, bit uaed coed yleni; a'r hwnn a uu garw ohonawch yrllyned, bit garnen eleni.”
sentences.l: “The one that was of-you as a-hind last-year, let-him-be a-boar of-the-wood this-year; and the one that was a-stag of-you last-year, let-him-be a-sow this-year.”
sentences.i: “The one of you who was a hind last year, let him be a wild boar this year; and the one of you who was a stag last year, let him be a sow this year.”
sentences.n: ohonawch 'of you', o conjugated (2 pl.). yrllyned 'last year' (modern y llynedd). bit 'let him be', 3 sg. imperative of bot, which softens what follows: uaed ← baed 'boar', garnen ← carnen 'sow'. baed coed 'boar of the wood', a wild boar. yleni and eleni 'this year' stand side by side, both spellings of the one word. The sexes are now crossed: the hind (Gilfaethwy) is to be the boar, the stag (Gwydion) the sow.

sentences.t: Ac ar hynny eu taraw a'r hutlath.
sentences.l: And on that their striking with the magic-rod.
sentences.i: And with that he struck them with the rod.
sentences.n: eu taraw 'their striking', struck them: eu 'their', the object before the verbal noun, causes no mutation. a'r 'with the'.

sentences.t: “Y mab hagen a gymerafi, ac a baraf y ueithryn a'y uedydyaw.”
sentences.l: “The boy, however, I it-is-that will-take, and that will-cause his rearing and his baptising.”
sentences.i: “The boy, however, I will take, and have him reared and baptised.”
sentences.n: Y mab, the object, is put first. hagen 'however'. a gymerafi is a gymeraf i 'I will take', kymeraf softened after a. a baraf 'I will cause'. y ueithryn ← meithryn 'rear', softened after y 'his'; a'y uedydyaw ← bedydyaw 'baptise', softened after 'y 'his'. The boy is the fawn.

sentences.t: Sef enw a dodet arnaw, Hydwn.
sentences.l: That-is the-name that was-put on-him: Hyddwn.
sentences.i: The name given him was Hyddwn.
sentences.n: a dodet 'that was put', the impersonal preterite (-et) of dodi. arnaw 'on him', ar conjugated (3 sg. masc.). Hydwn, Hyddwn, is from hyd 'stag' (d = /ð/).

sentences.t: “Ewch chwitheu, a bydwch y lleill yn uaed coed, a'r llall yn garnen coet. A'r anyan a uo y'r moch coet, bit y chwitheu. A blwydyn y hediw bydwch yma ydan y paret, ac ych etiued y gyt a chwi.”
sentences.l: “Go you-for-your-part, and be the one a boar of-the-wood, and the other a-sow of-the-wood. And the nature that may-be to the swine of-the-wood, let-it-be to you-for-your-part. And a-year from today be here under the wall, and your offspring together with you.”
sentences.i: “Go now, and be, the one a wild boar, the other a wild sow. Whatever nature the wild swine have, let it be yours. And a year from today be here beneath the wall, and your young with you.”
sentences.n: Ewch 'go', bydwch 'be', 2 pl. imperatives. y lleill is properly 'the others'; paired with a'r llall 'and the other' it stands for y naill 'the one' (the Red Book has y lleill too). yn uaed ← baed, yn garnen ← carnen, softened after the predicative yn. coed and coet are both written here, the same word. y'r 'to the'. moch coet 'swine of the wood', wild pigs. bit y chwitheu 'let it be to you'. ydan 'under', a form of adan. ych etiued 'your offspring'.

sentences.t: Ym penn y ulwydyn, llyma y clywyn kyuarthua cwn dan paret yr ystauell, a dygyuor y llys y am hynny am eu penn.
sentences.l: At the end of the year, behold they-heard(?) the-baying of-dogs under the wall of the chamber, and the-mustering of the court besides that about their head.
sentences.i: At the end of the year there came the baying of dogs beneath the chamber wall, and the court turning out about them as well.
sentences.n: y clywyn: so Evans. The Red Book has y clywynt 'they heard'; clywyn is either a slip for clywynt or for clywei 'he heard', as in the other two years. Kept as written. kyuarthua cwn 'the baying of dogs'. dygyuor 'mustering, gathering', the household turning out. y am hynny 'besides that' (or 'on account of that'; the sense is not certain). am eu penn 'about their head', around them.

sentences.t: Ar hynny kyuodi a oruc ynteu a mynet allan.
sentences.l: On that rising he-did he-for-his-part and going out.
sentences.i: At that he rose and went out.
sentences.n: The same pattern as the year before: kyuodi a oruc, then a mynet 'and going'.

sentences.t: A phan daw allan, trillydyn a welei.
sentences.l: And when he-comes out, three-beasts it-was-that he-saw.
sentences.i: And when he came out, he saw three beasts.
sentences.n: daw 'comes': the present tense in the past narrative, for vividness. trillydyn a welei: the object put first, then a and the verb; welei ← gwelei, softened after a.

sentences.t: Sef kyfryw lydnot a welei, baed coed, a charnen coet, a chrynllwdyn da y gyt ac wy.
sentences.l: That-is the-kind of-beasts that he-saw: a-boar of-the-wood, and a-sow of-the-wood, and a-good young-beast together with them.
sentences.i: These were the beasts he saw: a wild boar, a wild sow, and a fine young one with them.
sentences.n: kyfryw 'such, the kind of'. lydnot ← llydnot 'beasts', plural of llydyn, softened after kyfryw. a charnen ← carnen, a chrynllwdyn ← crynllwdyn, spirant after a. crynllwdyn: cryn 'considerable' + llwdyn 'young animal', a well-grown young beast. wy 'them'.

sentences.t: A breisc oed yn yr oet oed arnaw.
sentences.l: And stout he-was in the age that-was on-him.
sentences.i: And he was big for his age.
sentences.n: breisc 'thick, stout, big' (modern braisg), the predicate put first, then oed 'was'. yn yr oet oed arnaw 'in the age that was on him', for his age: age, like colour, is 'on' a creature.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb ef, “hwnn a gymerafi attaf, ac a baraf y uedydyaw.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said he, “this-one I it-is-that will-take to-me, and that will-cause his baptising.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said, “this one I will take to myself, and have him baptised.”
sentences.n: hwnn 'this one', the object put first. a gymerafi 'I will take', as before. attaf 'to me', at conjugated (1 sg.). y uedydyaw 'his baptising' (bedydyaw).

sentences.t: A'y daraw a'r hutlath yny uyd yn uab braswineu telediw.
sentences.l: And his striking with the magic-rod until he-is a boy stout-auburn handsome.
sentences.i: And he struck him with the rod, so that he became a fine boy, sturdy and auburn-haired.
sentences.n: A'y daraw 'and his striking': here taraw is softened after 'y 'his', as expected (contrast a'y taraw in col. 90). yn uab ← mab, softened after yn. braswineu: bras 'stout, thick' + gwineu 'auburn, chestnut', softened in the compound (the Red Book has the same compound); whether bras describes the boy or the depth of the colour is not certain. telediw 'handsome, well-made'.

sentences.t: Sef enw a dodet ar hwnnw, Hychdwn.
sentences.l: That-is the-name that was-put on that-one: Hychdwn.
sentences.i: The name given to that one was Hychdwn.
sentences.n: Hychdwn is from hwch 'pig, sow'. ar hwnnw 'on that one'.

sentences.t: “A chwitheu, yr un a uu baed coet ohonawch yrllyned, bit bleidast yleni; a'r hwnn a uu garnen yrllyned, bit uleid yleni.”
sentences.l: “And you-for-your-part, the one that was a-boar of-the-wood of-you last-year, let-him-be a-she-wolf this-year; and the one that was a-sow last-year, let-him-be a-wolf this-year.”
sentences.i: “And you: the one of you who was a wild boar last year, let him be a she-wolf this year; and the one who was a sow last year, let him be a wolf this year.”
sentences.n: A chwitheu 'and you for your part'. bit bleidast 'let him be a she-wolf': bleidast (bleid + -ast) is written unsoftened after bit, while bit uleid ← bleid follows; the scribe is not consistent (the Red Book softens both, bit uleidast … bit uleid). baed coet: coet here, coed in col. 91. Gilfaethwy, the boar, becomes the she-wolf; Gwydion, the sow, the wolf.

sentences.t: Ac ar hynny eu taraw a'r hutlath yny uydant bleid a bleidast.
sentences.l: And on that their striking with the magic-rod until they-are a-wolf and a-she-wolf.
sentences.i: And with that he struck them with the rod, so that they became a wolf and a she-wolf.
sentences.n: yny uydant 'until they were': uydant ← bydant, softened after yny. bleid a bleidast stand without yn (compare yny uyd yn garw).

sentences.t: “Ac anyan yr aniueileit yd ywch yn eu rith, bit y chwitheu. A bydwch yma blwydyn y'r dyd hediw ydan y paret hwnn.”
sentences.l: “And the-nature of-the animals that you-are in their form, let-it-be to you-for-your-part. And be here a-year to the day today under this wall.”
sentences.i: “And the nature of the beasts whose shape you wear, let it be yours. And be here a year from this very day, beneath this wall.”
sentences.n: aniueileit 'animals', plural of aniueil. yd ywch yn eu rith 'that you are in their shape': yd introduces the relative clause. blwydyn y'r dyd hediw 'a year to this day': Evans writes yr as one word (so too the Red Book); the word division is ours, and it is read y'r, y 'to' + 'r 'the'. ydan y paret hwnn 'under this wall'.

sentences.t: Yr un dyd ym penn y ulwydyn, llyma y chywei dygyuor a chyuarthua dan paret yr ystauell.
sentences.l: The same day at the end of the year, behold he-heard a-mustering and a-baying under the wall of the chamber.
sentences.i: On the same day at the end of the year, he heard a gathering and a baying beneath the chamber wall.
sentences.n: y chywei: a scribal slip for y clywei 'he heard' (Red Book clywei); the letters are certain on the image and kept as written. dygyuor 'mustering, gathering'. a chyuarthua ← kyuarthua, spirant after a.

sentences.t: Ynteu a gyuodes allan, a phan daw, llyma y guelei bleid, a bleidast, a chrubothon cryf y gyt ac wynt.
sentences.l: He-for-his-part it-was-that rose out, and when he-comes, behold he-saw a-wolf, and a-she-wolf, and a-strong cub(?) together with them.
sentences.i: He rose and went out, and when he came, there he saw a wolf, a she-wolf, and a strong cub with them.
sentences.n: Ynteu a gyuodes 'he rose': gyuodes ← kyuodes, 3 sg. preterite (-es) of kyuodi, softened after a. daw 'comes', the vivid present again. crubothon: a word found only here; the context makes it the young of the wolves, and 'cub' is the usual guess, but its formation is obscure and its meaning disputed. a chrubothon: spirant after a.

sentences.t: “Hwnn a gymeraf i,” heb ef, “ac a baraf y uedydyaw, ac y mae y enw yn parawt. Sef yw hwnnw, Bleidwn.
sentences.l: “This-one I it-is-that will-take,” said he, “and that will-cause his baptising, and there-is his name ready. That-is is that: Bleiddwn.
sentences.i: “This one I will take,” he said, “and have him baptised, and his name is ready to hand: it is Bleiddwn.
sentences.n: y mae y enw yn parawt 'his name is ready': y mae 'there is', parawt 'ready' after yn. Sef yw hwnnw 'that is it'. Bleidwn, Bleiddwn, is from bleid 'wolf'.

sentences.t: Y tri meib yssyd y chwi, a'r tri hynny ynt: Tri meib Giluaethwy enwir, tri chenryssedat kywir, Bleidwn, Hydwn, Hychdwn Hir.”
sentences.l: The three sons that-are to you, and those three are: Three sons of-Gilfaethwy false, three kenryssedat(?) true, Bleiddwn, Hyddwn, Hychdwn the-Tall.”
sentences.i: The three sons you have, these three are they: Three sons of Gilfaethwy the false, three warriors true: Bleiddwn, Hyddwn, Hychdwn the Tall.”
sentences.n: yssyd y chwi 'that are to you', that you have. ynt 'they are'. The last words are a three-line verse, rhyming enwir, kywir, Hir; Evans prints it as running text and it is kept in this unit. enwir 'false, wicked' (an- 'not' + gwir 'true'); kywir 'true, faithful'. The two rhyme-words are set against each other, but how kywir is meant (the sons true where their father was false, or simply 'true-born') is disputed. chenryssedat ← kenryssedat, spirant after tri: a word not found elsewhere in this form; 'warriors' is a guess from the context, but its meaning is disputed. The verse calls all three Gilfaethwy's sons, and by the tale they are: Hyddwn and Bleiddwn he bore himself, as the hind and the she-wolf, and Hychdwn, borne by Gwydion as the sow, he sired as the boar. Hir 'tall'.

sentences.t: Ac ar hynny yn y taraw wynteu yll deu a'r hutlath yny uydant yn eu cnawt eu hun.
sentences.l: And on that, in their striking they-for-their-part both-of-them with the magic-rod until they-are in their flesh their own.
sentences.i: And with that he struck them both with the rod, and they were in their own flesh again.
sentences.n: yn y taraw wynteu 'in their striking', striking them: y stands for eu 'their', and wynteu after the verbal noun repeats it. yll deu 'the two of them, both'. yny uydant 'until they were'. yn eu cnawt eu hun 'in their own flesh': cnawt 'flesh', eu hun 'their own'.

sentences.t: “A wyr,” heb ef, “o gwnaethauch gam ymi, digawn y buawch ym poen, a chywilyd mawr a gawssawch, bot plant o bob un ohonawch o'y gilid. Perwch enneint y'r gwyr, a golchi eu penneu, ac eu kyweiraw.”
sentences.l: “O men,” said he, “if you-did wrong to-me, enough you-have-been in pain, and great shame you-got, there-being children of each one of-you by the-other. Cause a-bath for the men, and washing their heads, and their making-ready.”
sentences.i: “Men,” he said, “if you have wronged me, you have been long enough in punishment, and great shame you have had, that each of you has had children by the other. Have a bath made ready for the men, and their heads washed, and see them dressed.”
sentences.n: A wyr 'O men': gwyr softened after the vocative a. o 'if' (later os); gwnaethauch, 2 pl. preterite of gwneuthur. gam ← cam 'wrong', softened as the object. digawn 'enough'. y buawch 'you have been', 2 pl. preterite of bot. ym poen 'in pain': yn + poen, the nasal mutation not shown on the p. a gawssawch ← kawssawch, 2 pl. preterite of kaffael, softened after a. bot plant 'there being children'. o bob un 'of each one': pob softened after o (the Red Book has y bop un 'to each one'). o'y gilid 'by his fellow', by the other (gilid ← kilid 'fellow'; modern ei gilydd). Perwch 'cause', 2 pl. imperative of peri. enneint 'bath'. a golchi: Evans prints agochi with the l raised over the word, brought into the line (Red Book golchi). kyweiraw 'make ready, dress'.

sentences.t: A hynny a berit udunt.
sentences.l: And that it-was-that was-caused for-them.
sentences.i: And that was done for them.
sentences.n: a berit 'was caused': berit ← perit, the impersonal imperfect (-it) of peri, softened after a. udunt 'for them'.

sentences.t: A guedy ymgueiraw ohonut, attaw ef y kyrchyssant.
sentences.l: And after making-themselves-ready by-them, to-him he it-was they-made-for.
sentences.i: And when they had made themselves ready, they went to him.
sentences.n: guedy 'after' with the verbal noun ymgueiraw 'make oneself ready' (ym- + kyweiraw). At the end of the line Evans prints a repeated y dotted beneath, the scribe's cancellation, so it is left out. ohonut: so Evans, without the second n, for ohonunt 'by them' (Red Book ohonunt), giving the doer of the verbal noun; a short dotted mark under the o is read as a mark, not a cancellation, but the reading is uncertain. attaw ef y kyrchyssant 'to him they went': the phrase put first, then y and the verb.

sentences.t: “A wyr,” heb ef, “tangneued a gawsawch, a cherennyd a geffwch. A rodwch im kynghor pa uorwyn a geisswyf.”
sentences.l: “O men,” said he, “peace you-have-got, and friendship you-will-get. And give to-me counsel what maiden I-should-seek.”
sentences.i: “Men,” he said, “you have had peace, and you shall have friendship. Now give me counsel: what maiden should I seek?”
sentences.n: tangneued a gawsawch 'peace you have got': the object first; gawsawch is written with one s here, gawssawch in col. 92 just before. a cherennyd ← kerennyd 'friendship', spirant after a. a geffwch ← keffwch, 2 pl. present-future of kaffael, softened. rodwch 'give', 2 pl. imperative of rodi. pa uorwyn ← morwyn, softened after pa 'what'. a geisswyf ← keisswyf, 1 sg. present subjunctive (-wyf) of keissaw, 'that I should seek'.

sentences.t: “Arglwyd,” heb y Guydyon uab Don, “hawd yw dy gynghori. Aranrot uerch Don, dy nith uerch dy chwaer.”
sentences.l: “Lord,” said Gwydion son of Dôn, “easy is your counselling. Aranrhod daughter of-Dôn, your niece, daughter of your sister.”
sentences.i: “Lord,” said Gwydion son of Dôn, “you are easily counselled: Aranrhod daughter of Dôn, your niece, your sister's daughter.”
sentences.n: hawd yw 'easy it is'. dy gynghori 'your counselling', to counsel you: kynghori softened after dy. Aranrot is Aranrhod (r for rh, t = /d/). uerch ← merch 'daughter', softened after the name. nith 'niece'.

sentences.t: Honno a gyrchwyt attaw.
sentences.l: She it-was-that was-fetched to-him.
sentences.i: She was brought to him.
sentences.n: Honno 'that one (fem.)', she. a gyrchwyt 'was fetched': gyrchwyt ← kyrchwyt, the impersonal preterite (-wyt) of kyrchu, softened after a.

sentences.t: Y uorwyn a doeth ymywn.
sentences.l: The maiden it-was-that came in.
sentences.i: The maiden came in.
sentences.n: Y uorwyn ← morwyn, softened after the feminine article. ymywn 'in, inside' (yn + mywn).

sentences.t: “A uorwyn,” heb ef, “a wyt uorwyn di?”
sentences.l: “O maiden,” said he, “are you a-maiden you?”
sentences.i: “Maiden,” he said, “are you a maiden?”
sentences.n: A uorwyn 'O maiden': morwyn softened after the vocative a. a wyt 'are you?': the question particle a + wyt 'you are'. uorwyn, the complement, softened. di 'you', the pronoun after the verb.

sentences.t: “Ny wnn ni amgen no'm bot.”
sentences.l: “I-know-not I other than my being.”
sentences.i: “I know no other than that I am.”
sentences.n: wnn ← gwnn 'I know', 1 sg. present of gwybot, softened after Ny. ni: so Evans, certain on the image. It is apparently the pronoun i with the n of wnn written twice (Red Book y wnn i arglwyd amgen nom bot; the second witness Ny wnn i); kept as written. amgen 'otherwise, other'. no'm 'than my': no 'than' + 'm 'my'; bot 'being'.

sentences.t: Yna y kymerth ynteu yr hutlath a'y chamu.
sentences.l: Then he-took he-for-his-part the magic-rod and its bending.
sentences.i: Then he took the rod and bent it.
sentences.n: y kymerth 'he took'. a'y chamu 'and its bending', bent it: 'y 'her, it' (llath is feminine) gives the spirant mutation, camu > chamu. camu 'bend' sounds like camu 'step', the verb of the next sentence; the play on the two may be meant.

sentences.t: “Camha di dros honn,” heb ef, “ac ot wyt uorwyn, mi a ednebydaf.”
sentences.l: “Step you over this,” said he, “and if you-are a-maiden, I it-is-that will-know.”
sentences.i: “Step over this,” he said, “and if you are a maiden, I shall know.”
sentences.n: Camha 'step', 2 sg. imperative of camu/camhu. di 'you'. dros 'over'. honn 'this (fem.)', the rod. ot 'if', the form of o/os before wyt. a ednebydaf 'I will know', 1 sg. present-future of adnabot 'recognise'.

sentences.t: Yna y camawd hitheu dros yr hutlath, ac ar y cam hwnnw adaw mab brasuelyn mawr a oruc.
sentences.l: Then she-stepped she-for-her-part over the magic-rod, and at that step leaving a big stout-yellow boy she-did.
sentences.i: Then she stepped over the rod, and at that step she dropped a big, sturdy, yellow-haired boy.
sentences.n: y camawd 'she stepped': the 3 sg. preterite in -awd (modern -odd). hitheu 'she for her part'. ar y cam hwnnw 'at that step': cam 'a step'. adaw … a oruc 'leaving she did': adaw is 'leave (behind), let fall'. brasuelyn: bras 'stout' + melyn 'yellow, fair', softened in the compound.

sentences.t: Sef a wnaeth y mab, dodi diaspat uchel.
sentences.l: That-is what the boy did: putting a-cry loud.
sentences.i: What the boy did was give a loud cry.
sentences.n: Sef a wnaeth … dodi 'what he did was putting'. diaspat 'cry, shriek'; dodi diaspat 'put out a cry'. uchel 'loud, high'.

sentences.t: Yn ol diaspat y mab, kyrchu y drws a oruc hi, ac ar hynny adaw y ryw bethan ohonei.
sentences.l: After the-cry of the boy, making-for the door she-did, and on that leaving a kind-of little-thing from-her.
sentences.i: At the boy's cry she made for the door, and as she did so some small thing dropped from her.
sentences.n: Yn ol 'after'. kyrchu y drws a oruc hi 'making for the door she did'. adaw again, 'leaving, dropping'. y ryw bethan 'some kind of little thing': ryw 'kind', and bethan ← pethan (peth 'thing' + the diminutive -an), softened after ryw. ohonei 'from her', o conjugated (3 sg. fem.).

sentences.t: A chyn cael o neb guelet yr eil olwc arnaw, Guydyon a'y kymerth, ac a droes llen o bali yn y gylch, ac a'e cudyawd.
sentences.l: And before getting by anyone seeing the second look on-it, Gwydion it-was-that took-it, and that turned a-sheet of brocade around it, and that hid-it.
sentences.i: And before anyone could get a second look at it, Gwydion took it, wrapped a sheet of brocade about it, and hid it.
sentences.n: A chyn ← kyn 'before', spirant after a. cael o neb guelet 'anyone's getting to see': o neb gives the doer of cael. yr eil olwc 'the second look': eil 'second', and olwc ← golwc 'look', softened after it. arnaw 'on it' (masc.): the Red Book has arnei 'on her'; the White Book is kept, 'on it', the thing. a'y kymerth 'took it': the infixed 'y 'him, it' leaves kymerth unmutated. a droes ← troes 'turned', softened after a. llen 'sheet, cloth'. o bali ← pali 'brocade, silk', softened after o. yn y gylch 'around it' (kylch). a'e cudyawd 'and hid it': 'e is another spelling of the infixed 'y; cudyawd, 3 sg. preterite (-awd) of cudyaw.

sentences.t: Sef y cudyawd, ymywn llaw gist is traed y wely.
sentences.l: That-is where he-hid-it: inside a hand-chest below the feet of his bed.
sentences.i: Where he hid it was in a small chest at the foot of his bed.
sentences.n: Sef y cudyawd 'that is, he hid it': y is the verbal particle. ymywn 'inside'. llaw gist 'hand-chest', a small chest: gist ← kist, softened after llaw in the compound. is traed y wely 'below the feet of his bed': y wely ← gwely, softened after y 'his'.

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb mab Mathonwy, “mi a baraf uedydyaw hwn,” wrth y mab brasuelyn.
sentences.l: “Yes,” said the-son of-Mathonwy, “I it-is-that will-cause baptising this-one,” to the boy stout-yellow.
sentences.i: “Yes,” said the son of Mathonwy, “I will have this one baptised” — meaning the sturdy yellow-haired boy.
sentences.n: heb mab Mathonwy 'said the son of Mathonwy', that is, Math. The White Book has no name here (Red Book heb y math mab mathonwy; the second witness's [Math uab] is Williams's supplement); nothing is supplied, since the phrase reads as it stands. uedydyaw ← bedydyaw, softened as the object of baraf. wrth 'to, with regard to'.

sentences.t: “Sef enw a baraf, Dylan.”
sentences.l: “That-is the-name that I-will-cause: Dylan.”
sentences.i: “The name I shall give him is Dylan.”
sentences.n: Sef enw a baraf 'the name I will cause (to be given)', the same frame as Sef enw a dodet above.

sentences.t: Bedydyaw a wnaethpwyt y mab, ac y gyt ac y bedydywyt, y mor a gyrchwys.
sentences.l: Baptising was-done the boy, and as-soon-as he-was-baptised, the sea it-was-that he-made-for.
sentences.i: The boy was baptised, and as soon as he was baptised he made for the sea.
sentences.n: Bedydyaw a wnaethpwyt y mab 'baptising was done the boy': the verbal-noun pattern with the impersonal wnaethpwyt, the boy standing after as its object. y gyt ac y 'as soon as'. y bedydywyt 'he was baptised', impersonal preterite (-wyt). y mor a gyrchwys 'the sea he made for': the object put first.

sentences.t: Ac yn y lle, y gyt ac y doeth y'r mor, annyan y mor a gauas, a chystal y nouyei a'r pysc goreu yn y mor; ac o achaws hynny y gelwit Dylan Eil Ton.
sentences.l: And in the place, as-soon-as he-came to the sea, the-nature of the sea he-got, and as-good he-would-swim as the fish best in the sea; and because of that he-was-called Dylan Eil Ton.
sentences.i: And at once, as soon as he came to the sea, he took on the sea's nature, and swam as well as the best fish in the sea; and for that he was called Dylan Eil Ton.
sentences.n: yn y lle 'in the place', at once. y'r mor 'to the sea'. annyan is anyan 'nature', spelt with nn. a gauas 'he got': gauas ← kauas, preterite of kaffael, softened after a. a chystal ← kystal 'as good', the equative of da, spirant after a; a'r 'as the' after the equative. y nouyei 'he would swim', imperfect of nouyaw. o achaws hynny 'because of that'. y gelwit 'he was called': gelwit, the impersonal imperfect (-it) of galw. Dylan Eil Ton: ton 'wave'; eil is 'second' or 'son, offspring', and whether the name means 'Dylan Son of Wave', 'Dylan Second Wave' or something else is disputed; it is left in Welsh.

sentences.t: Ny thorres tonn adanaw eiryoet.
sentences.l: There-broke-not a-wave under-him ever.
sentences.i: No wave ever broke beneath him.
sentences.n: Ny thorres ← torres 'broke', 3 sg. preterite (-es) of torri, spirant after Ny. tonn 'wave', written ton just before. adanaw 'under him', adan conjugated (3 sg. masc.). eiryoet 'ever'.

sentences.t: A'r ergyt y doeth y angheu ohonaw, a uyrywys Gouannon y ewythyr.
sentences.l: And the blow that came his death from-it, it-was-that cast Gofannon his uncle.
sentences.i: And the blow from which his death came was cast by Gofannon, his uncle.
sentences.n: A'r ergyt 'and the blow, the cast' (of a thrown weapon) is put first; y doeth y angheu ohonaw 'that his death came from it': ohonaw 'from it', o conjugated (3 sg. masc.). a uyrywys ← byrywys 'cast', 3 sg. preterite (-wys) of bwrw, softened after a; its subject Gouannon comes after. Gouannon is Gofannon (u = /v/). The Red Book has the same words but the other preterite ending, a uyryawd. y ewythyr 'his uncle'. Nothing more is told of the death.

sentences.t: A hwnnw a uu trydyd anuat ergyt.
sentences.l: And that it-was-that was the-third ill-fated blow.
sentences.i: And that was one of the Three Ill-fated Blows.
sentences.n: a uu 'was', preterite of bot, softened after a. trydyd 'third': the triad formula, 'the third (of three)', that is, one of a set of three Ill-fated Blows; the other two are not named here. anuat: an- 'not' + mat 'lucky, good', softened in the compound; whether it means 'unlucky', 'ill-fated' or 'wicked' is disputed. The part ends here, at col. 94 l. 10; the next begins on the same line.
